conviction_note: The full-year raise is all but certain (yen about 8% weaker than the 147 plan through H1; profit raised at the last two H1 prints, which reacted +7.4/+11.3 on estimated dates). But IFIS consensus already sits about 9% above the plan, and the company habitually keeps its H2 FX assumption conservative, so the size of the raise relative to the street is a coin flip with a slight positive tilt. The tilt comes from the dividend-payout path and this name's positive H1 reactions, offset by a 27x margin-long overhang. Findings sum +1.8 against a scaled +0.66 (p_up 56, abs 5.5); the gap is the sign uncertainty, which belongs in p_up.
bar: H1 ordinary profit consensus 24,000m JPY and FY ordinary consensus 39,875m (kabuyoho/IFIS, data 2026-10-09, https://kabuyoho.jp/report?bcode=6432), against company plan H1 22,600m / FY 36,500m (Q1 tanshin 2026-07-10, https://tdnet-pdf.kabutan.jp/20260710/140120260710591084.pdf). Only one estimate source (IFIS via kabuyoho) was reachable; no 四季報 number found, so the bar has one consensus source and the company plan.
positioning_check: JPX disclosed short register: 0.0%, no position at or above 0.5%, unchanged (as of 2026-09-29, https://www.jpx.co.jp/markets/public/short-selling/index.html). 信用倍率 27.24x (margin sell 19.1k, buy 520.3k shares at 10/02 per kabutan https://kabutan.jp/stock/?code=6432), i.e. about 3 days of turnover sitting margin-long. findings.finding: The yen ran far weaker through H1 (Mar-Aug 2026) than the plan assumes: USD/JPY about 155-163 (roughly 159 average) against a plan of 147, EUR/JPY about 177-187 against 174, GBP/JPY about 206-219 against 200. Takeuchi has revised its full year at every H1 print since at least 2022, and kept a deliberately conservative H2 rate each time (2024: H2 USD 138 against an H1 actual of 154.54; 2025: 140 against 146.74). So an upward FY revision at this release is very likely. Its size against a street already 9% above plan is the open question.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: H1 prints with an FY profit raise: 2024-10-10 (op +15.6%) moved +7.42% and 2025-10-10 (op 33.6 to 38.0bn plus a 10 yen dividend raise) moved +11.32%. Both dates come from the baseline's estimated cadence, and kabutan's articles confirm a +ve reaction on 2025-10-14 ('大幅反発'). The Jul 2026 Q1 print, plan held and op in line with consensus, moved +2.81%.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: IFIS FY ordinary 39,875 sits about 9% above plan, so the street already marks a raise. What is not in the price is how far the company goes, given that its documented habit is to keep H2 FX at least 7-16 yen below spot. If the market had fully priced a raise to the street level, the stock would trade near the 8,633 consensus target rather than at 13.2x company EPS. It has been range-bound at 7,000-7,900 since April.
findings.independence: FX levels: Yahoo monthly FX bars (https://query1.finance.yahoo.com/v8/finance/chart/JPY=X?range=1y&interval=1mo). Plan rates: FY tanshin 2026-04-10 (https://assets.finboard.net/tdnet-filings/20260410501419.pdf). The 2024 H2-rate habit: https://www2.jpx.co.jp/disc/64320/140120241010596312.pdf. Different documents, one thesis.

findings.finding: The company's stated return policy targets a 40% consolidated payout, 'raised in stages'. The current 220 yen plan on 560.69 EPS is a 39.2% payout, and at the 2025 H1 print the company raised the dividend 10 yen alongside the profit raise. Any EPS raise therefore mechanically implies a dividend increase above 220 at this release.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: 2026-04-10: a new interim dividend and +10 yen drew '後場終盤に急騰' (+9.98% on the estimated date). 2025-10-10: +10 yen together with the profit raise drew +11.32%. Both are joint with the guidance line.
findings.why_not_priced: Consensus is quoted on profit, not on the dividend. A retail-heavy register (margin ratio 27x) reacts to the 増配 headline itself. If it were priced, the yield would not sit at 2.96% on the 220 plan. Cash fell 28.7bn in Q1 on working capital, so a buyback is unlikely and the dividend is the lever.
findings.independence: Dividend history: kabutan finance page (https://kabutan.jp/stock/finance?code=6432). The April 2026 interim-dividend reaction: https://kabutan.jp/stock/news?code=6432&b=n202604100803. Same policy, different documents.

findings.finding: Q1 orders of 90.3bn (+59.2%) rested on one 'まとまった受注' from a large US rental company. Q2 standalone orders will very likely fall sharply quarter on quarter and the end-August backlog shrink from 77.1bn. The last time orders fell QoQ (Jan 2026, Q3 orders -10.7% QoQ, backlog -49.5% YoY), the stock fell 7.87%. The company has also said it stops disclosing orders after this fiscal year.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: 2026-01-13: orders down QoQ moved -7.87% (fisco: '受注高が前四半期比で大幅減'). 2026-07-10: orders +59% moved +2.81%, then '大幅続伸' the next day.
findings.why_not_priced: The lumpiness was disclosed in July, so the decline is inferable and largely held by the price. What is not priced is the headline: a QoQ order drop printed beside a raise is what fisco/kabutan wrote up negatively in January. H1 cumulative orders will still be up strongly YoY (about 135bn against about 99bn), which cushions it.
findings.independence: Jan 2026 reaction article: https://kabutan.jp/stock/news?code=6432&b=n202601140380. A different document, the same order series.

findings.finding: United Rentals raised gross rental capex guidance by $450m to $4.85-5.25bn on 2026-07-22, citing historically high time utilisation. That supports H2 US unit demand for Takeuchi, whose Q1 orders came from a large US rental company, and so supports the volume side of any FY revision.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: no Takeuchi-specific history for a counterparty read-through; the stock rose about 9% from 7,130 (7/10) to 7,770 (7/27) across the Q1 print and the URI release.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: it has been public since July. It is filed small because it is a counterparty proxy, and the customer is not named in Takeuchi's filing.
findings.independence: Q1 tanshin names a US large rental company order (https://tdnet-pdf.kabutan.jp/20260710/140120260710591084.pdf).

findings.finding: Takeuchi bore 5,138m JPY of US tariff cost in FY2026/2 (Mar 2025-Feb 2026), when its products were under the IEEPA reciprocal tariff; the 25% steel-derivative 232 duty only began 2026-04-06. The Supreme Court voided IEEPA tariffs on 2026-02-20, and CBP's CAPE refunds opened 2026-04-20, with about 70% of claims approved by mid-July. A refund recognised in Q2 would lift H1 below-op or one-off lines. No Takeuchi-specific disclosure was found, and the Q1 tanshin is silent.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: none for this line on this name
findings.why_not_priced: Neither consensus nor the company plan mentions a refund; if it were expected, the H1 net consensus would sit above the plan by more than FX alone explains. It is a one-off with no path to the guide, so it is sized at a fraction of the money.

baseline_tension: The findings lean positive against a baseline lean of -0.86 (margin overhang) and a flat run-up (+2.75% over 20d, -0.8% over 5d). The strongest positive the release could carry (an FY raise plus a dividend raise) was looked for and is the core of the file. The strongest negative is a raise smaller than the 9%-above-plan consensus, together with a QoQ order drop, landing on 27x margin longs.
lessons_applied: Rule 1 (a negative resting on data already in the last 短信): the Q2 order-drop finding rests on the July disclosure that the Q1 order was a one-off lump, so it was shrunk from -0.6 to -0.4
Rule 2 (negatives outnumbering positives): not triggered, since one negative sits against four positives; baseline_tension records the strongest negative as well
